'''Francisco José Ayala Pereda''' (March 12, 1934 – March 3, 2023) was a Spanish-American [[evolutionary biologist]] and philosopher who was a longtime faculty member at the [[University of California, Irvine]], and [[University of California, Davis]].<ref>{{cite book | author= Pinar García, Susana | title= De Dios y ciencia. La evolución de Francisco J. Ayala | year= 2016 | publisher= Alianza Editorial | location= Madrid | isbn= 9788491042358}}</ref>

Ayala was previously president and chairman of the board of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/04/29/science/29prof.html | title=Roving Defender of Evolution, and of Room for God  |work=New York Times | date=April 29, 2008  | access-date =April 24, 2009 | first=Cornelia | last=Dean}}</ref> At University of California, Irvine, his academic appointments included [[University Professorship (University of California)|University Professor]] and Donald Bren Professor of Biological Sciences, Ecology & Evolutionary Biology (School of Biological Sciences), Professor of Philosophy (School of Humanities), and Professor of Logic and the Philosophy of Science (School of Social Sciences).<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.the-scientist.com/article/display/16880/ | title=Biologist Francisco J. Ayala |publisher=[[The Scientist (magazine)|The Scientist]] | date=February 5, 1996 | access-date =April 24, 2009}}</ref>

Ayala's employment at UC Irvine ended in 2018 after the university issued a report relating to allegations of [[sexual harassment]] claims against him.<ref name=ScienceFelled>{{Cite news|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/report-gives-details-sexual-harassment-allegations-felled-famed-geneticist|title=Here's the sexual harassment report that felled a famed geneticist—and his defense|date=2018-07-20|work=Science|publisher=AAAS|author=Meredith Wadman}}</ref> Ayala denied having "intentionally caused sexual harassment to anybody."<ref name=ScienceFelled/> His name was removed from the [[UCI School of Biological Sciences|School of Biological Sciences]], the Science Library, as well as various graduate fellowships, scholarship programs, and endowed chairs.<ref name=newname/>

==Early life and education==
Earlier in life, Ayala was a [[Dominican Order|Dominican]] priest,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/evolution/religion/faith/statement_01.html |title=Evolution: Religion: Science and Faith |publisher=Pbs.org |access-date=July 26, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/04/27/science/conversation-with-francisco-j-ayala-ex-priest-takes-blasphemy-evolution.html | title=A CONVERSATION WITH: FRANCISCO J. AYALA; Ex-Priest Takes the Blasphemy Out of Evolution |work=New York Times | date=April 27, 1999 | access-date =April 24, 2009 | first=Claudia | last=Dreifus | author-link=Claudia Dreifus }}</ref> ordained in 1960 and leaving the priesthood that same year.<ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Richardson | first1 = W. | last2 = Slack | first2 = Gordy | title = Faith in science: scientists search for truth | year = 2001 | publisher = Routledge | location = London | isbn = 0-415-25765-4 | page = [https://archive.org/details/faithinsciencesc0000unse/page/6 6] | url = https://archive.org/details/faithinsciencesc0000unse/page/6 }}</ref> After graduating from the [[University of Salamanca]], he moved to the United States in 1961 to study for a PhD at [[Columbia University]]. There, he studied for his doctorate under [[Theodosius Dobzhansky]], graduating in 1964.<ref>{{cite journal | title=Theodosius Dobzhansky: The Man and the Scientist |journal=[[Annual Review of Genetics]] | date=1976| first=Francisco | last=Ayala | pmid=797305 | doi=10.1146/annurev.ge.10.120176.000245 | volume=10 | pages=1–6}}</ref> He became a [[US citizen]] in 1971.

==Career==
Ayala is known for his research on population and evolutionary genetics, and has been called the "[[Polymath|Renaissance Man]] of Evolutionary Biology".<ref name="AAASInterview">{{cite news | url=http://www.aaas.org/programs/centers/pe/events/20060323ayala.shtml | title=A Conversation with Hana and Francisco J. Ayala | publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] | date=March 23, 2006 | access-date=April 24, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090605165750/http://www.aaas.org/programs/centers/pe/events/20060323ayala.shtml | archive-date=June 5, 2009 | df=mdy-all }}</ref> His "discoveries have opened up new approaches to the prevention and treatment of diseases that affect hundreds of millions of individuals worldwide", including demonstrating that the reproduction of ''[[Trypanosoma cruzi]]'', the agent of [[Chagas disease]], is mostly the product of cloning, and that only a few clones account for most of this widespread disease.<ref name="UniversityMedal"/>

Ayala served on the advisory board of the now defunct [[Campaign to Defend the Constitution]], an organization that has lobbied in support of the [[separation of church and state]].  He has been publicly critical of U.S. restrictions on federal funding of [[embryonic stem cell]] research. He was also a critic of [[intelligent design]] theories, claiming that they are not only [[pseudoscience]], but also misunderstood from a [[theology|theological]] point of view. He suggested that the theory of [[evolution]] resolves [[the problem of evil]], thus being a kind of [[theodicy]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Ayala|first1=F. J.|title=Darwin's Gift to Science and Religion|date=2007|publisher=[[Joseph Henry Press]]|location=[[Washington, D.C.]]|page=xi|quote=I shudder in terror at the thought that some people of faith would implicitly attribute this calamity to the Creator's faulty design. I rather see it as a consequence of the clumsy ways of the evolutionary process..}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Ayala|first1=F. J.|title=Darwin's Gift to Science and Religion|date=2007|publisher=[[Joseph Henry Press]]|location=[[Washington, D.C.]]|pages=4{{endash}}5|quote=Later, when I was studying the theology in Salamanca, Darwin was a much-welcomed friend. The theory of evolution provided the solution to the remaining component of the problem of evil. As floods and drought were a necessary consequence of the fabric of the physical world, predators and parasites, dysfunctions and diseases were a consequence of the evolution of life. They were ''not'' a result of a deficient or malevolent design: the features of organisms were not ''designed'' by the Creator.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Ayala|first1=F. J.|title=Darwin's Gift to Science and Religion|url=https://archive.org/details/darwinsgifttosci00ayal|url-access=limited|date=2007|publisher=[[Joseph Henry Press]]|location=[[Washington, D.C.]]|page=[https://archive.org/details/darwinsgifttosci00ayal/page/n162 159]|quote=Religious scholars in the past had struggled with imperfection ... in the living world, which [is] difficult to explain if [it is] the outcome of God's design. ... Evolution came to the rescue. ... The theory of evolution, which at first had seemed to remove the need for God in the world, now has convincingly removed the need to explain the world's imperfections as failed outcomes of God's design.}}</ref> Although Ayala generally did not discuss his religious views, he has stated that "science is compatible with religious faith in a personal, omnipotent and benevolent God."<ref name="New Scientist interview with Ayala, Apr 2010">{{cite web| first= Graham|last= Lawton|date= 2 April 2010|title=Templeton prizewinner: We need science plus morality|work=New Scientist|url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg20627546.800-templeton-prizewinner-we-need-science-plus-morality.html}}</ref> He also briefly served, in 1960, as a Dominican priest.<ref>Ruse, Michael. Can a Darwinian Be a Christian? : The Relationship between Science and Religion. Cambridge University Press: New York, xi + 242 pp. 2001, p. 75</ref> Ayala did not say whether he remained a religious believer, not wanting to be "tagged by one side or the other."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dean|first1=Cornelia|title=Roving Defender of Evolution|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/04/29/science/29prof.html|work=New York Times|date=April 29, 2008|quote=Dr. Ayala does not say whether he remains a religious believer. "I don't want to be tagged,” he said. "By one side or the other.”}}</ref> Ayala served as an expert witness in ''[[McLean v. Arkansas]] Board of Education,'' a court case that overturned the mandatory teaching of creationism alongside evolution in grade school science classes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Francisco J. Ayala {{!}} Biography, Books, & Facts {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Francisco-J-Ayala |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref>

Ayala attended the [[Beyond Belief: Science, Religion, Reason and Survival|Beyond Belief]] symposium in November 2006. Ayala debated [[Christian apologist]] [[William Lane Craig]] in November 2009 on the topic of intelligent design.<ref>{{cite web |title=Is Intelligent Design Viable? The Craig-Ayala Debate |url=https://www.reasonablefaith.org/media/debates/is-intelligent-design-viable-craig-ayala-debate/ |website=reasonablefaith.org |access-date=2 August 2018}}</ref>

On October 18, 2011, the University of California, Irvine (UCI) announced that Ayala would be donating $10 million to the university's School of Biological Sciences. The gift was to be "$1 million a year for the next decade."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.latimes.com/news/local/la-me-uci-gift-20111018,0,2845450.story?track=rss |url-status=dead |work=Los Angeles Times |first=Carla |last=Rivera |title=UC Irvine professor donating $10 million to school |date=October 18, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111018162336/http://www.latimes.com/news/local/la-me-uci-gift-20111018,0,2845450.story?track=rss |archive-date=October 18, 2011 }}</ref>

==Sexual harassment investigation==
Four women (professor [[Kathleen Treseder]], another professor, an assistant dean, and one graduate student),<ref name=Wadman>Meredith Wadman, [https://www.science.org/content/article/prominent-geneticist-out-uc-irvine-after-harassment-finding Prominent geneticist out at UC Irvine after harassment finding], ''Science'' (June 29, 2018).</ref> alleged that Ayala had sexually harassed them, prompting an investigation led by Erik Pelowitz at UC Irvine's Office of Equal Opportunity and Diversity.<ref name=ScienceFelled/> The university investigators concluded that Ayala violated the university's policies on sexual harassment and sex discrimination in the cases of three of the four women,<ref name=ScienceFelled/> and found that the conduct at issue extended to 2004 and had led to previous warnings to Ayala.<ref name=ScienceFelled/> The investigators' report also concluded that Ayala "engaged in a campaign with the highest University officials to influence the outcome of this investigation."<ref name=ScienceFelled/>  Ayala denied most allegations against him, and wrote to the university's chancellor, [[Howard Gillman]], "I have never intentionally caused sexual harassment to anybody. To the extent that my actions may have caused harm to others ... I apologize from the deepest of my heart and of my mind."<ref name=ScienceFelled/> He resigned effective July 1, 2018.<ref name=Wadman/>

Ayala was represented in the investigation by attorney [[Susan Estrich]].<ref name="Wadman" /> The investigation against Ayala extended to more than 60 witnesses,<ref name="Wadman" /> and the outcome divided scholars.<ref name="ScienceFelled" /><ref name="Wadman" /> [[Camilo José Cela Conde]]<ref name="Wadman" /> and [[Elizabeth Loftus]] defended him, the latter saying that she was "shocked that this man's life was ruined over this collection of reactions to his behavior" and described the allegations as "thin."<ref name="ScienceFelled" /> In contrast, [[T. Jane Zelikova]], the founder of [[500 Women Scientists]], supported Ayala's ouster.<ref name="ScienceFelled" /> [[Ann Olivarius]], a lawyer and sexual harassment expert who reviewed the report at the request of ''Science'' magazine, said that Ayala did not "have sex with students or pressure them directly for sex" but "clearly made multiple women feel degraded" and continued to do so "after senior university officials warned him to stop acting in these ways."<ref name="ScienceFelled" />

Ayala returned to his private life, and the university removed his name from the School of Biological Sciences, the Science Library, and endowed chairs that had been named after Ayala.<ref name=newname>{{cite web|url=https://news.uci.edu/2018/06/28/uci-proposes-new-name-for-school-of-biological-sciences-science-library-after-internal-investigation-substantiates-sexual-harassment-claims-against-signature-donor/|title=UCI proposes new name for School of Biological Sciences, science library after internal investigation substantiates sexual harassment claims against signature donor|work=UCI News|date=June 28, 2018}}</ref><ref name=LAT2018>{{cite news |last1=Watanabe |first1=Teresa |title=Acclaimed UC Irvine geneticist resigns after committing sexual harassment |url=http://www.latimes.com/local/education/la-me-edu-uc-irvine-ayala-sexual-harassment-20180628-story.html |access-date=29 June 2018 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=28 June 2018}}</ref> The [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] removed his [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|fellowship status]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Wadman|first=Meredith|date=2018-09-21|title=AAAS adopts new policy for ejecting harassers|journal=Science|language=en|volume=361|issue=6408|pages=1175|doi=10.1126/science.361.6408.1175|issn=0036-8075|pmid=30237333|bibcode=2018Sci...361.1175W|s2cid=206626401}}</ref> The U.S. National Academy of Sciences rescinded Ayala's membership for violation of Section 4 of the NAS Code of Conduct, effective June 23, 2021.<ref name=NAS>{{cite journal|last1=Ortega|first1=Rodrigo Pérez|title=National Academy of Sciences ejects biologist Francisco Ayala in the wake of sexual harassment findings|date=June 24, 2021|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/national-academy-sciences-ejects-biologist-francisco-ayala-wake-sexual-harassment|journal=Science|access-date=24 June 2021}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
In 2001, Ayala was awarded the [[National Medal of Science]].<ref name="UniversityMedal">{{cite news | url=http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/4322 | title=Biologist Francisco J. Ayala Wins National Medal of Science | publisher=[[University of California]] | date=May 9, 2002 | access-date=April 24, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905000326/http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/4322 | archive-date=September 5, 2008 | df=mdy-all }}</ref> On April 13, 2007, he was awarded the first of 100 bicentennial medals at [[Mount St. Mary's University (Maryland)|Mount Saint Mary's University]] for lecturing there as the first presenter for the Bicentennial Distinguished Lecture Series. His lecture was entitled "The Biological Foundations of Morality". Other awards he received include the Gold Honorary Gregor Mendel Medal of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]], the Gold Medal of the Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei, the Gold Medal of the [[Stazione Zoologica]] in Naples, the President's Award of the [[American Institute of Biological Sciences]], the [[AAAS Award for Scientific Freedom and Responsibility]]<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ufggAQAAMAAJ&q=%22Stanley+L+Weinberg%22+%22award%22 |title=The Scientist |date=1987 |publisher=Institute for Scientific Information |volume=1 |pages=27 |language=en |issue=4–27}}</ref> and 150th Anniversary Leadership Medal of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS]], the Medal of the [[College of France]], the UCI Medal of the University of California, the 1998 Distinguished Scientist Award from the [[SACNAS]], and [[Sigma Xi]]'s William Procter Prize for Scientific Achievement, 2000. In 2010, he was awarded the [[Templeton Prize]].<ref name="Templeton">{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/26/science/26templeton.html | title=Biologist Wins Templeton Prize  |work=New York Times | date=March 25, 2010 | access-date =March 25, 2010 | first=Cornelia | last=Dean}}</ref>  The science library at UCI was named after him from 2010 until 2018, when his name was removed after a university investigation concluded that his conduct with respect to three women violated university policies.<ref name=ScienceFelled/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lib.uci.edu/features/news/francisco-ayala-science-library.html|title=UCI Science Library to be named in honor of Francisco J. Ayala|date=April 26, 2010|access-date=May 4, 2010|publisher=University of California, Irvine|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120525164556/http://www.lib.uci.edu/features/news/francisco-ayala-science-library.html|archive-date=May 25, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref name="LAT2018" /> Ayala delivered a lecture at the [[Trotter Prize (Texas A&M)|Trotter Prize]] ceremony in 2011 entitled "Darwin's Gift to Science and Religion." In 2014, UCI named its School of Biological Sciences the Francisco J. Ayala School of Biological Sciences after Ayala.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://give.uci.edu/recognition/news/uc-irvines-school-of-biological-sciences-renamed-in-honor-of-francisco-j-ayala.php|title=UC Irvine's School of Biological Sciences renamed in honor of Francisco J. Ayala|access-date=21 March 2014|archive-date=March 22, 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140322022722/http://give.uci.edu/recognition/news/uc-irvines-school-of-biological-sciences-renamed-in-honor-of-francisco-j-ayala.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> UCI removed his name from the library and school in 2018, after finding that he sexually harassed at least four women.<ref name="LAT2018" />

Ayala was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1977, and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1980, though his fellowship status in these institutions was later revoked.<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter A|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=April 28, 2011}}</ref> He was a member of the [[American Philosophical Society]]. He was also a foreign member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], the [[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]] in Rome, the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]], the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]], and the [[Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts]]. He had honorary degrees from the [[University of Athens]], the [[University of Bologna]], the [[University of Barcelona]], the [[University of the Balearic Islands]], the [[University of León]], the [[Autonomous University of Madrid|University of Madrid]], the [[University of Salamanca]], the [[University of Valencia]], the [[University of Vigo]], [[Far Eastern National University]], [[Masaryk University]] and [[University of Warsaw]].

== Personal life ==
Francisco Ayala was born to Francisco Ayala and Soledad Pereda. In the late 1960s he met Mary Henderson, they married on May 27, 1968.<ref>{{cite web | title=Dr. Francisco Ayala y Pereda Fiance of Miss Mary Henderson | website=NYTimes.com | date=1968-03-10 | url=https://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1968/03/10/90031529.html?pageNumber=89 | access-date=2026-03-15}}</ref> They had two sons: Francisco José (born 1969) and Carlos Alberto (born 1972).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/4322|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905000326/http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/4322 |archive-date=September 5, 2008 |title=Biologist Francisco J. Ayala Wins National Medal of Science|website=University of California |date=2002-05-09|author1=Vasich, Tom|df=mdy-all}}</ref> Their marriage ended in divorce,<ref>{{cite web |title=Templeton Prize Fact Sheet |url=http://www.templetonprize.org/pdfs/2010_prize/A-FactSheet.pdf |access-date=June 29, 2010 |archive-date=April 11, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120411060701/http://www.templetonprize.org/pdfs/2010_prize/A-FactSheet.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in 1985 he married an ecologist named [[Hana Ayala]] (née Lostáková, born 1956).<ref name="AAAS2">{{cite web |url=http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2006/0331ayala.shtml |title=Hana and Francisco J. Ayala: Separate Careers, a Common Passion for Knowledge|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|date=31 March 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110708020044/http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2006/0331ayala.shtml |archive-date=July 8, 2011 |df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |editor=Elizabeth Sleeman | title = The International Who's Who 2004 | year = 2003 | publisher = Routledge | isbn = 1-85743-217-7 | page = 83 | url-access = registration | url=https://archive.org/details/internationalwho2004ond/page/83 }}</ref> They lived in [[Irvine, California]]. He died from a heart attack on March 3, 2023, in Newport Beach, at age 88.<ref>{{cite news |title=Muere el genetista Francisco J. Ayala a los 88 años de edad |url=https://elpais.com/ciencia/2023-03-05/muere-el-genetista-francisco-j-ayala-a-los-88-anos-de-edad.html |access-date=6 March 2023 |publisher=El País |date=5 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| last= Dean| first= Cornelia| title= Francisco Ayala, Biologist and Defender of Evolution, Dies at 88| url= https://www.nytimes.com/2023/03/10/science/francisco-ayala-dead.html| date= 10 March 2023| work= [[The New York Times]]| accessdate= 11 March 2023| archive-date= March 10, 2023| archive-url= https://archive.today/20230310184504/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/03/10/science/francisco-ayala-dead.html| url-status= bot: unknown}}</ref>

== Books ==
Ayala has published 950 publications and 30 books. Recently published books include:
*Ayala, F.J. ''Evolution, Explanation, Ethics and Aesthetics: Towards a Philosophy of Biology''. Academic Press: 2016. {{ISBN|9780128036938}}
*Ayala, F.J. ''Am I a Monkey: Six Big Questions About Evolution''. Johns Hopkins University Press: Baltimore, MD, US 2010.
*Ayala, F.J. and [[Robert Arp]], eds. ''Contemporary Debates in Philosophy of Biology''. Wiley-Blackwell: London, 2009. {{ISBN|978-1-4051-5998-2}}
*Avise, J.C. and F.J. Ayala, eds. ''In the Light of Evolution: Adaptation and Complex Design''. National Academy Press: Washington, DC. 2007. {{ISBN|978-0-309-10405-0}}
*[[Camilo José Cela Conde|Cela Conde, C.J.]] and F.J. Ayala. ''Human Evolution. Trails from the Past''. Oxford University Press: Oxford, 2007.
*Ayala, F.J. Darwin y el Diseño Inteligente. ''Creacionismo, Cristianismo y Evolución''. [[Alianza Editorial]]: Madrid, Spain, 231 pp.&nbsp;2007.
*Ayala, F.J. ''Darwin's Gift to Science and Religion''. Joseph Henry Press: Washington, DC, xi + 237 pp.&nbsp;2007
*Ayala, F.J. ''La Evolución de un Evolucionista. Escritos Seleccionados''. University of Valencia: Valencia, Spain, 441 pp.&nbsp;2006. {{ISBN|84-370-6526-7}}
*Ayala, F.J. ''Darwin and Intelligent Design''. Fortress Press: Minneapolis, MN, xi + 116 pp.&nbsp;2006.
*Ayala, F.J. and [[Camilo José Cela Conde|C.J. Cela Conde]]. ''La piedra que se volvió palabra. Las claves evolutivas de la humanidad''. Alianza Editorial: Madrid, Spain. 184 pp.&nbsp;2006 {{ISBN|84-206-4783-7}}
*Hey, J., W.M. Fitch and F.J. Ayala, eds. ''Systematics and the Origin of Species. On Ernst Mayr's 100th Anniversary''. National Academies Press: Washington, DC. xiii + 367 pp.&nbsp;2005 {{ISBN|0-309-09536-0}}
*[[Franz M. Wuketits|Wuketits, F.M.]] and F.J. Ayala, eds. ''Handbook of Evolution: The Evolution of Living Systems (Including Hominids), Volume 2''. Wiley-VCH: Weinheim, Germany. 292 pp.&nbsp;2005. {{ISBN|978-3-527-61971-9}}
*Ayala, F.J. ''Le Ragioni dell’ Evoluzione''. Di Renzo Editore: Rome. 109 pp.&nbsp;2005.
*Ayala, F.J. ''Human Evolution: Biology, Culture, Ethics''. In: J.B. Miller, ed., The Epic of Evolution. Science and Religion in Dialogue (Pearson Education, Inc.: Upper Saddle River, New Jersey), pp.&nbsp;166–180. 2004.
